findings.text: Emulator provides an internal segment installation service that takes a selector and destination register, resolves the table entry through host callbacks, enforces mode and privilege constraints, and either installs the validated descriptor or delivers a processor fault.
Table location handling observes a pointer abstraction with size plus address members, while segmented memory handling observes an address abstraction with segment plus offset members.

Operand handling observes a discriminated abstraction with kind plus width plus value storage and address variants covering register, memory, string range and vector forms with associated count and data references.

Each protected mode table entry spans eight bytes with bounds requiring coverage of the indexed slot, and selector value encodes index in upper bits with table choice and privilege in low bits where the lowest four values count as null.
Absolute memory encoding selects immediate width from current address size, using two byte, four byte and eight byte immediates for sixteen, thirty two and sixty four bit address sizes respectively.

Real mode segment handling preserves cached attributes while deriving base from selector paragraph, and virtual mode data handling creates fresh present writable descriptors with full narrow limit and user privilege.

Code installation enforces distinct privilege checks for conforming and nonconforming types across call, return and task switch transfers, preventing escalation and inner returns while aligning stored privilege with current privilege.

Stack handling requires writable data with matching privilege, task register handling requires available system kind, local table handling requires its dedicated system kind, and remaining data handling rejects unsuitable code kinds and privilege above descriptor privilege.

Missing present indication yields stack fault for stack and not present fault otherwise, first use of present code or data persists accessed indication via table store, and sixty four bit system handling validates extended base legality before install.

When control protection with shadow stacks is active on a sixty four bit host, transition out of sixty four bit execution is rejected when the shadow pointer retains nonzero upper half or when required host state is unavailable.

Segment installation proceeds through fetch, privilege and type validation, optional persistence of accessed or busy state, then host install, with validation failures diverting to a single fault exit carrying vector plus code and transport failures aborting without install.
Task register installation performs an atomic compare exchange on the table entry to set busy state, so concurrent table writers serialize on the entry contents rather than overwriting.

Segmented accesses linearize before invoking host memory operations, and emulated reads stage bytes through an internal cache that replays in order across re emulation and survives caller stack reuse, treating overflow as beyond emulation scope.
Bit operations targeting memory with register count relocate the target by whole bytes from high count bits and keep only the residual sub word offset for the element operation.

Port string input prefetches a bounded burst constrained by remaining count, cache room and page remainder with direction awareness, then either publishes the burst as a string operand or serves single elements from cache.

Interrupt descriptor fetch obtains the current table pointer from the host, checks bounds for the indexed slot, then issues a system read for the full entry or raises a protection fault with the selector derived code.
Host offers dedicated write entry points for extended, legacy and media vector widths that manage floating point context internally and then store to the architectural register file.

Guest vector stores must hold the host floating point context across the raw register update via paired acquisition and release around each write, with no assumption of persistence across separate writes.
Raw vector selection supports low registers on all hosts and extended registers only on sixty four bit hosts for wide and legacy widths, while media width supports eight registers.
Out of range raw vector selection is treated as a host bug rather than a recoverable guest fault, so callers must guarantee architectural validity of the index beforehand.

Result commitment dispatches on operand kind to register, memory, string range or vector destination, using atomic compare exchange for locked memory, plain store otherwise, scaled length for strings, and upper lane clearing for legacy vector writes.

Stack push reserves space before storing via the stack segment and pop loads before releasing, masked to stack width, with frame, segment register and bulk register helpers built from those primitives plus descriptor reload and shadow state handling.

Flag push stores current flags with virtual indication cleared, while flag restore from stack allows only a privilege and mode dependent subset to change and rejects underprivileged virtual mode attempts.
Correct replay of staged memory and port bytes depends on deterministic re decode in original order after host exits, since cached data is consumed positionally rather than by address.
Real mode interrupt handling starts by capturing current flags and preparing table pointer plus code and offset fetch state for the vector target.
